transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Amir Patel (Redwood CSM), Jordan Kim (Acme CTO), Priya Singh (Acme SRE), Tom Alvarez (Acme Data Eng), Sofia Moreno (Acme PM)

Summary / Highlights: Lena quick recap, Marcus gives bench plan, Priya clarifies network and security, action items and next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — just want to confirm folks on the line?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Yep this is Jordan, we good.
00:15 Speaker 1 (Lena): Great. Marcus, Amir, you want to do quick intros?
00:20 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Marcus Li, infra/performances, I'll lead the bench. Sorry, performances, infra, stream, you know.
00:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya Singh, SRE — I'm the one who'll set up VPC peering and service accounts.
00:35 Speaker 1 (Lena): Awesome. Agenda: onboarding progress, access setup, env readiness, benchmarks, next steps.
00:42 Speaker 5 (Tom): Quick note — we've been running internal tests on a smaller toy model and want the POC to exercise 2k token sequences.
00:50 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Perfect, we'll do a 2k seq benchmark with 8 concurrent clients initially, adjust as needed.
01:05 Speaker 1 (Lena): On onboarding, I sent the org invite and API keys to Sofia last week — Sofia did you get them?
01:12 Speaker 6 (Sofia): Yes I got the invite but can't access private buckets yet, I got a 403 when trying to upload prompts.
01:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): That sounds like an IAM or bucket policy; Tom and I will share the bucket policy and cross-account roles.
01:25 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Also we need KMS integration, we can't have plaintext keys in the platform.
01:32 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Redwood supports customer KMS through the Private deployment path; for Hosted we can do envelope encryption but if you require customer-managed KMS we should look at Private or Dedicated with KMS peering.
01:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): For compliance we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and retention for a year. Is that possible?
01:52 Speaker 1 (Lena): Yes — Redwood Console supports audit export; we'll include the steps in the security pack.
02:00 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Quick note on perf: if you hit token lengths at 2k with batching, kernel selection and kv cache warmup matter a lot. We'll configure continuous batching but keep tail latency SLO in mind.
02:12 Speaker 5 (Tom): What's a realistic p95 latency target we can expect for 2k seq?
02:20 Speaker 3 (Marcus): On Dedicated 8x A100-ish or equivalent, p95 generation could be around 650-900 ms per turn depending on model. On Hosted lower tiers might be higher, e.g., 1.2s to 2s. These are ballpark — bench will confirm.
02:40 Speaker 1 (Lena): We should also measure cost per 1k tokens — Redwood Optimize will give quantization suggestions to reduce unit cost.
02:48 Speaker 4 (Priya): Important: we can't expose PHI to any third party. We'll need to confirm data residency and that logs can be redacted before export.
02:56 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Understood. For Private we can keep everything in your VPC and route logs to your SIEM. For Hosted we have redaction options but it might be limited; we'll include redaction patterns in the security doc.
03:10 Speaker 1 (Lena): Action items: Marcus to run bench, Lena to send SOC2/security pack, Priya to share network details. Does that sound right?
03:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yep. Also, can Redwood provide a temporary bastion user for initial setup or should we spin our own?
03:26 Speaker 3 (Marcus): You can spin your own; we'll provide the steps. If you want Redwood to create a service account in your account for peering we can do that with least privilege.
03:35 Speaker 5 (Tom): Follow-up question on model variants: we want to try quantized 4-bit and a float baseline — will the runtime handle fallbacks automatically if quantization causes unexpected outputs?
03:48 Speaker 3 (Marcus): We have automatic fallbacks in routing policies — you can set a rollout that fails over to the float baseline if quality drops below threshold. We'll demo that in the next tech deep dive.
04:01 Speaker 1 (Lena): On the procurement side Jordan, any timeline for sign-off?
04:07 Speaker 2 (Jordan): We're aiming for an internal decision in early August, so we need the bench results and security artifacts before that.
04:15 Speaker 6 (Sofia): I also asked for a cheat-sheet for quick integration — SDK snippets, curl examples for upload, prompting best practices.
04:22 Speaker 3 (Marcus): We'll share a quickstart repo and a sample scoring script.
04:30 Speaker 1 (Lena): Competitors — Jordan asked about Anthropic and OpenAI cost comparisons? Jordan did you want Redwood pricing vs them?
04:38 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Just context — we trialed OpenAI for prototyping, but cost and residency are blockers. We're evaluating Redwood if we can hit latency and compliance.
04:52 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Performance aside, Redwood's Dedicated option gives predictable throughput and SLA that helps in production. We'll include rough cost-model numbers post-bench.
05:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): Network specifics: we'll provide CIDR for peering and create a cross-account role. How do you prefer the service account information?
05:15 Speaker 1 (Lena): Put it in the shared Confluence page and also email it to me. We'll sync with your infra.
05:22 Speaker 3 (Marcus): For benchmarking we'll need: sample payload distribution (Tom to provide), expected QPS, seq length distribution, and any auth headers.
05:32 Speaker 5 (Tom): I'll export a week of anonymized traffic tomorrow.
05:36 Speaker 1 (Lena): Great. Anything else?
05:40 Speaker 6 (Sofia): One more: can we get a short runbook for failure modes — e.g., if model node OOMs, what happens to requests?
05:48 Speaker 3 (Marcus): We'll include that in the ops doc — fallback policies, autoscaling and retries.
05:52 Speaker 1 (Lena): Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
05:56 Speaker 3 (Marcus): I'll run the benchmark starting Monday, share an initial spreadsheet with latency + cost per 1k tokens.
06:01 Speaker 1 (Lena): I'll email the SOC2 and security pack and a network diagram by Friday.
06:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll provide VPC peering CIDR and create the role by Thursday.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Jordan): We'll review bench results internally and set up the dedicated sizing call.
06:20 Speaker 1 (Lena): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Confluence and schedule the dedicated call for next week.
06:28 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Thanks, bye.
06:30 End of recording.

Notes on transcription: a few words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'performances' for 'performance', 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'kay vee cache'). There are short overlaps in speakers around 03:25-03:35.

References mentioned (links noted): Security pack (link sent after meeting), Quickstart repo (github.com/redwood/quickstart - placeholder), Benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared by Marcus).
